subject: Math
prompt: The height, in feet, of a ball $t$ seconds after it is launched straight up in the air can be modeled by the function $g(t) = -16t^{2} + 24t + 6$. Based on the model, which of the following statements best interprets the equation $g(0.5) = 14$?

choices.A: The height of the ball $0.5$ seconds after being launched straight up in the air is $14$ feet.
choices.B: The height of the ball $14$ seconds after being launched straight up in the air is $0.5$ feet.
choices.C: The height of the ball $14$ seconds after being launched straight up in the air is approximately $0.5$ times as great as its initial height.
choices.D: The speed of the ball $0.5$ seconds after being launched straight up in the air is approximately $14$ feet per second.

explanation:
Choice A is correct. The value $0.5$ is the value of $t$, which represents the number of seconds after the ball was launched straight up in the air. When the function $g$ is evaluated for $t = 0.5$, the function has a value of $14$, which is the height, in feet, of the ball.

Why C is incorrect:

Choice C is incorrect and may result from misidentifying seconds as feet and feet as seconds. Additionally, choice C may result from incorrectly comparing the value of the function to the initial height of the ball.
